sourceShortSummaries: The party investigates a recently abandoned campsite outside the ruined Dunmari fort and follows its owner's tracks toward the causeway.
An ankheg erupts beneath Wellby during his reconnaissance of the fort, but the party frees him and kills the creature.
The party examines the ankheg's lair, discovers extensive animal traffic into the caves, and chooses to rest in the pentagonal building.
sourceLongSummaries: After reviewing their earlier fight with hobgoblin skeletons, the party examines the foundations outside the fort. They find a concealed, human-sized campsite with scattered food, a shovel, and gear left behind but no weapons or water. Tracks connect the camp to the disturbed burial mound and lead into the fort without returning, suggesting that the missing camper entered prepared for danger and never came back.

Wellby crosses the causeway alone and scouts the ruined headquarters, cistern, towers, and pentagonal building while a large chittering creature moves inside the central ruin. As the others approach, Delwath recognizes the signs of a burrowing desert predator, but an ankheg bursts from below and seizes Wellby. Seeker undermines its rear legs with Mold Earth, Kenzo strikes its mandibles until it releases Wellby, and Delwath delivers the killing blow with his longsword.

The party confirms that the ankheg was behaving with unusual daytime aggression, then searches the ruined headquarters where it had been feeding on a lion. A sloping natural passage beneath the ruin contains signs of lions, hyenas, lizards, and other creatures moving in both directions. With the air still and the hour just after lunchtime, the party postpones entering the caves and heads toward the intact pentagonal building for shelter and a short rest.

sourceShortSummaries: The party rests in the magically preserved Dunmari temple, recovers sacred objects, and finds an enchanted horn in a ruined tower.
Underground, the party finds the petrified Arcus and a Chardonian coin that transforms into a floating disc.
The party discovers a cockatrice nursery where hatchlings repeatedly petrify a trapped lion, then retreats to explore the other tunnel.
The wider tunnel leads beneath the ruined cistern, where the party follows the old watercourse toward the source of the disturbance.
A wave of unnatural rage and three animated skeletons confront the party at the entrance to the southern cavern.
An undead hobgoblin wielding an obsidian-topped staff joins the battle, but the party overwhelms it and captures the staff.
The party studies the malignant staff, connects it tentatively to Cha'mutte, and finds a flaw that may allow the obsidian to be destroyed.
sourceLongSummaries: The pentagonal building proves to be a temple to the Five Siblings whose enchanted walls have survived the fort's destruction. The party identifies and takes Aagir's Everlight, gathers portable religious relics, and completes a short rest in the temple's calming atmosphere. Searching the gate towers afterward, Wellby finds the old remains of a Dunmari scout or outrider and recovers a magical horn decorated with a running-horse motif before the party prepares to descend underground.

The party descends through the ankheg's tunnel into a junction where they find an extraordinarily lifelike stone man missing one arm, with a broken stone torch nearby. The recent condition of the statue and its waterskin connect it to the abandoned campsite, although the party does not yet know Arcus's name. A heavy old Chardonian coin lying nearby radiates transmutation magic; when Seeker flips it, it unfolds into a hovering disc that follows him and can carry weight before returning to coin form.

Following the narrower branch, the party reaches a muddy chamber containing cockatrice hatchlings, eggs, and a lion that repeatedly turns to stone and back as the hatchlings peck it. They watch unseen long enough to identify the creatures and consider whether the cockatrices also petrified Arcus. Unwilling to provoke the hatchlings or risk meeting their parents while Seeker is low on magic, they withdraw to the junction and choose the wider passage toward the detected obsidian.

The party retreats to the statue chamber and follows the wider branch into a cavern beneath the cracked cistern, where midafternoon light shines through the collapsed floor. After a brief pause, they continue south along the dry watercourse while debating whether the fort's geological damage, altered animals, and detected obsidian share a magical source. They conclude that Arcus may have been another investigator rather than the cause and press cautiously toward a larger cavern.

As Delwath reaches the cavern entrance, an unseen influence briefly freezes him and three skeletons drop from the ceiling to attack. Delwath recognizes that the source of the animals' rage is nearby, then holds the narrow front while the others fight from behind him. He destroys one skeleton with a Hex-enhanced longsword blow, while Seeker uses the Floating Disc Coin as an improvised barrier and the party continues battling the remaining undead.

A rotting hobgoblin carrying a black iron staff crowned with pulsing obsidian enters the cavern, claims the power as its own, and repeatedly projects waves of rage and dark energy. The party finishes the remaining skeletons and turns on the new foe: Delwath curses it, Seeker and Wellby attack from range, and Kenzo closes in despite the staff's magical defenses. Wellby's hidden shot badly wounds it, and Kenzo finally strikes it down, leaving the still-radiating staff on the cavern floor.

Although its bearer is dead, the obsidian staff continues radiating rage, and its inscription speaks of binding others to an unnamed power. Searching the cavern reveals older petrified animals and a necklace whose winged-flame symbol Delwath associates with Cha'mutte's Great War armies. The party theorizes that the staff—not necessarily its undead wielder—drove the surrounding animals mad, while Seeker identifies a structural flaw in the obsidian. They debate moving it outside before Delwath warns that exposing it could spread its influence farther.

sourceShortSummaries: The party shatters the obsidian, ends its maddening influence, and rests overnight before returning toward camp the next morning.
sourceLongSummaries: As agitated insects gather, the party commits to destroying the staff in the cavern. Kenzo uses Aagir's Everlight as a wedge against the flaw, suffering psychic backlash when his blow cracks the obsidian; Seeker's ordinary tools fail against its magical defenses, but Wellby widens the fracture despite further backlash. Delwath finally shatters it with a shadowy summoned blade, releasing the oppressive rage and calming the nearby animals. The party collects the now-mundane obsidian and necklace, plans to bring Arcus's petrified body into the temple, rests overnight, and finds the desert calmer when they head back toward camp on March 26.

A heavy old Chardonian coin lying nearby radiates transmutation magic; when Seeker flips it, it unfolds into a hovering disc that follows him and can carry weight before returning to coin form.

Following the narrower branch, the party reaches a muddy chamber containing cockatrice hatchlings, eggs, and a lion that repeatedly turns to stone and back as the hatchlings peck it. They watch unseen long enough to identify the creatures and consider whether the cockatrices also petrified Arcus. Unwilling to provoke the hatchlings or risk meeting their parents while Seeker is low on magic, they withdraw to the junction and choose the wider passage toward the detected obsidian.

The party retreats to the statue chamber and follows the wider branch into a cavern beneath the cracked cistern, where midafternoon light shines through the collapsed floor. After a brief pause, they continue south along the dry watercourse while debating whether the fort's geological damage, altered animals, and detected obsidian share a magical source. They conclude that Arcus may have been another investigator rather than the cause and press cautiously toward a larger cavern.

recapBlocks.title: Battle for the Obsidian
sourceShortSummaries: A wave of unnatural rage and three animated skeletons confront the party at the entrance to the southern cavern.
An undead hobgoblin wielding an obsidian-topped staff joins the battle, but the party overwhelms it and captures the staff.
sourceLongSummaries: As Delwath reaches the cavern entrance, an unseen influence briefly freezes him and three skeletons drop from the ceiling to attack. Delwath recognizes that the source of the animals' rage is nearby, then holds the narrow front while the others fight from behind him. He destroys one skeleton with a Hex-enhanced longsword blow, while Seeker uses the Floating Disc Coin as an improvised barrier and the party continues battling the remaining undead.

A rotting hobgoblin carrying a black iron staff crowned with pulsing obsidian enters the cavern, claims the power as its own, and repeatedly projects waves of rage and dark energy. The party finishes the remaining skeletons and turns on the new foe: Delwath curses it, Seeker and Wellby attack from range, and Kenzo closes in despite the staff's magical defenses. Wellby's hidden shot badly wounds it, and Kenzo finally strikes it down, leaving the still-radiating staff on the cavern floor.

recapBlocks.title: Breaking the Staff
sourceShortSummaries: The party studies the malignant staff, connects it tentatively to Cha'mutte, and finds a flaw that may allow the obsidian to be destroyed.
The party shatters the obsidian, ends its maddening influence, and rests overnight before returning toward camp the next morning.
sourceLongSummaries: Although its bearer is dead, the obsidian staff continues radiating rage, and its inscription speaks of binding others to an unnamed power. Searching the cavern reveals older petrified animals and a necklace whose winged-flame symbol Delwath associates with Cha'mutte's Great War armies. The party theorizes that the staff—not necessarily its undead wielder—drove the surrounding animals mad, while Seeker identifies a structural flaw in the obsidian. They debate moving it outside before Delwath warns that exposing it could spread its influence farther.

As agitated insects gather, the party commits to destroying the staff in the cavern. Kenzo uses Aagir's Everlight as a wedge against the flaw, suffering psychic backlash when his blow cracks the obsidian; Seeker's ordinary tools fail against its magical defenses, but Wellby widens the fracture despite further backlash. Delwath finally shatters it with a shadowy summoned blade, releasing the oppressive rage and calming the nearby animals. The party collects the now-mundane obsidian and necklace, plans to bring Arcus's petrified body into the temple, rests overnight, and finds the desert calmer when they head back toward camp on March 26.
